chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muawiyah ibn Hakim, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from al-Fadl ibn Yasar, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) say:

Whoever drinks wine and gets drunk from it, his prayer will not be accepted for forty days. If he refrains from prayer during these days, the punishment will be doubled for him for leaving the prayer. And in another tradition: Indeed, the prayer of the wine-drinker is suspended between the heaven and the earth; when he repents, it is returned to him.

key_terms.بَيْنَ السَّمَاءِ وَالْأَرْضِ: Between the heaven and the earth

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the prayers of someone who drinks wine and gets drunk?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), establishing a forty-day period where the prayers of an intoxicated person are suspended, a duration often linked to the time it takes for the body's impurities to settle. The narration highlights the severity of neglecting prayer during this window, warning of intensified punishment, while offering hope that sincere repentance restores the spiritual connection, allowing prayers to ascend from their suspended state between heaven and earth.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 22-1 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted Muawiyahibn Hakim, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of Aban ibn Uthman, on the authority of Al-Fuzayl ibn Yasar that he had heard Aba Ja’far al-Baqir (MGB) say, “

The prayers of whoever drinks wine would not be accepted for forty days. If he doesn’t say his prayers during these forty days, he will suffer an extra chastisement for not saying his prayers.In another tradition we read, “The prayers of whoever drinks would be wandering between the heavens and the Earth. They are ascribed to him once he repents.”
